zh.title: 独立开发者出海：从 0 到 1 上线并收款的 SaaS
zh.subtitle: 一个人也能跑通：选题验证、最小架构、登录计费、Stripe 收款、上线与首批用户
zh.tagline: 不教你写 CRUD，而是教你把「一个想法」变成「有付费用户的在线产品」的完整商业链路。
audience: 有开发能力，但不知道做什么、怎么验证需求的独立开发者
已经在做副业项目，卡在「上线了没人付费」阶段的人
想从外包 / 接单转向产品化收入的工程师
小团队创始人：需要一套可复用的上线与收款基础设施
outcomes: 用 2 周完成选题验证，避免花 3 个月做一个没人要的产品
搭出能扛住第一批 1000 用户的最小技术架构（不做过早优化）
实现多租户登录、订阅计费、额度限制与升级/降级流程
用 Stripe 完成全球收款：Checkout、订阅、优惠码、税务与退款
完成上线清单：域名、邮件、监控、法务页与首屏转化
拿到前 10 个付费用户的可复制获客动作
deliverables: SaaS 启动模板：Next.js App Router + 认证 + Stripe 订阅 + 额度中间件
定价页与 5 种定价模型对照表
上线前 60 项检查清单（技术 / 支付 / 法务 / 增长）
冷启动渠道清单：20 个可直接发帖的社区与打法

modules.title: 模块 1 · 选题与需求验证
lessons: 三种适合独立开发者的产品形态：工具、垂直 SaaS、信息产品
从自己的痛点里挖需求：问题清单法
用 5 个页面验证需求（不等产品写完）
预售与等待名单：用真实付款意图替代点赞

modules.title: 模块 2 · 最小技术架构
modules.summary: 目标是「能上线、能收钱、能改」，不是「能支撑百万用户」。
lessons: 技术选型：Next.js / Remix / Astro 的选择标准
数据库与 ORM：Postgres + Prisma / Drizzle 的最小约定
认证方案：Auth.js、Clerk、Supabase Auth 的成本与迁移风险
部署与成本：Vercel、Cloudflare、Fly.io 的免费额度边界
可观测性：日志、错误追踪、用量埋点一次配好

modules.title: 模块 3 · 多租户与权限
modules.summary: 租户模型设计错了，后面每一步都疼。
lessons: 单库多租户 vs 独立 schema：什么时候该选哪个
组织 / 成员 / 邀请：最小可用的团队模型
权限设计：角色、资源、动作三层模型
额度与限流：免费用户的成本护栏

modules.title: 模块 4 · Stripe 收款与定价
modules.summary: 支付是产品功能，不是「接个按钮」。
lessons: Stripe 账户准备：主体、KYB、结算币种与手续费
Checkout Session vs Payment Link vs 自建表单：怎么选
订阅模式：试用、按席位、按用量与混合计费
Webhook 与订单状态机：支付成功不等于开通成功
优惠码、早鸟价与退款策略
Stripe Tax / 发票 / 多币种：出海必须处理的细节
对账：把 Stripe 付款记录和你的用户表对上

modules.title: 模块 5 · 上线
modules.summary: 上线是一份清单，不是一次点击。
lessons: 域名、DNS、邮件域名（SPF/DKIM/DMARC）一次配对
落地页结构：首屏、社会证明、定价、FAQ
法务三件套：隐私政策、服务条款、退款政策
上线前演练：用真实测试卡跑通支付全链路
灰度与回滚：出问题时怎么把损失控制在一小时内

modules.title: 模块 6 · 首批用户与增长
modules.summary: 前 100 个用户靠手，不靠广告。
lessons: 冷启动渠道盘点：Product Hunt、Reddit、HN、垂直社区
内容 SEO：用 10 篇对比文拿下长尾搜索
转化优化：定价页 A/B 与取消流程挽留
从免费到付费：触发升级的 4 个时机

modules.title: 模块 7 · 运营与合规
modules.summary: 能长期收款，才算真的上线。
lessons: 退款、拒付（chargeback）与风控处理流程
数据合规：GDPR / CCPA 的最小实现
收入记账与税务申报的基础认知
什么时候该注册海外主体，什么时候不该

faq.q: 我没有海外公司，可以用 Stripe 吗？
faq.a: Stripe 需要对应国家/地区的合法主体。课程会对比「香港/新加坡/美国主体 + Stripe」与「Paddle / Lemon Squeezy 等 Merchant of Record」两条路径的成本、合规责任与适用阶段，帮你选一条能走通的路。
需要基础的 React / TypeScript。模板仓库会给你一个能跑的应用，你主要工作是改业务逻辑和接自己的产品。
会讲付费投放的时机与最小预算测试，但重点放在免费/低成本渠道，因为独立开发者的现金流更脆弱。

faq.q: 适合已经有产品的人吗？
faq.a: 适合。模块 4（收款）和模块 5（上线）可以单独吸收；如果你卡在「有流量没转化」，模块 6 会有直接帮助。
会持续更新。Stripe API、认证服务和部署平台的变更都会同步到课件与模板仓库，已购用户免费获取。

seo.description: 面向独立开发者的出海实战课：需求验证、最小架构、多租户登录、Stripe 订阅收款、上线清单与首批付费用户获客，30 节课跑通完整商业链路。

instructor.name: OpenCode Guide 课程组
instructor.role: 独立产品与支付集成实战经验
instructor.bio: 课程内容来自多个自研产品的真实上线记录：踩过的 Stripe 坑、被拒付的订单、以及最后真正带来收入的那几个渠道。

zh.guarantee: 7 天无理由退款：先看模块 1 和 4，觉得不适合就退。

en.title: Indie SaaS Launch: From Idea to Paid Customers
en.subtitle: Validate, build, charge and launch a SaaS as a team of one
en.tagline: Not another CRUD tutorial — the full commercial path from idea to paying users.
audience: Developers who can build but don't know what to build or how to validate it
Side-project builders stuck at 'launched, nobody pays'
Freelancers moving from hourly work to product revenue
Small founders who need a reusable launch and billing foundation
outcomes: Validate an idea in two weeks instead of building for three months
Ship a minimal architecture that survives your first 1,000 users
Implement multi-tenant auth, subscription billing, quotas and plan changes
Take payments globally with Stripe: Checkout, subscriptions, coupons, tax, refunds
Complete a launch checklist: domain, email, monitoring, legal pages, conversion
Run a repeatable playbook for your first ten paying customers
deliverables: SaaS starter repo: Next.js App Router + auth + Stripe subscriptions + quota middleware
Pricing page and a comparison of five pricing models
A 60-item pre-launch checklist (engineering / payments / legal / growth)
Cold-start channel list: 20 places to post with concrete angles

modules.title: Module 1 · Idea and validation
lessons: Three product shapes that fit indie developers: tools, vertical SaaS, info products
Mine your own pain: the problem inventory method
Validate with five pages, before the product exists
Pre-orders and waitlists: real payment intent beats likes

modules.title: Module 2 · Minimal architecture
modules.summary: You need launchable, chargeable and changeable — not infinite scale.
lessons: Stack selection: Next.js, Remix or Astro
Database and ORM: Postgres with Prisma or Drizzle, minimal conventions
Auth: Auth.js, Clerk, Supabase Auth — cost and lock-in tradeoffs
Deploy and cost: the real limits of Vercel, Cloudflare and Fly.io free tiers
Observability: logs, error tracking and usage analytics in one pass

modules.title: Module 3 · Multi-tenancy and permissions
modules.summary: Get the tenant model wrong and every later step hurts.
lessons: Shared schema vs schema-per-tenant: when to pick which
Organisations, members and invites: the minimal team model
Permissions: roles, resources and actions
Quotas and rate limits: cost guardrails for free users

modules.title: Module 4 · Stripe and pricing
modules.summary: Payments are product work, not a button.
lessons: Stripe account setup: entity, KYB, settlement currency, fees
Checkout Sessions vs Payment Links vs custom forms
Subscription models: trials, per-seat, usage-based and hybrid
Webhooks and order state machines: payment success ≠ access granted
Coupons, early-bird pricing and refund policy
Stripe Tax, invoices and multi-currency
Reconciliation: matching Stripe payouts to your user table

modules.title: Module 5 · Launch
modules.summary: Launching is a checklist, not a click.
lessons: Domains, DNS and email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
Landing page anatomy: hero, proof, pricing, FAQ
The legal trio: privacy policy, terms, refund policy
Launch rehearsal with real test cards and a full payment run
Staged rollout and rollback: capping damage to one hour

modules.title: Module 6 · First users and growth
modules.summary: Your first hundred users come from hand-to-hand work.
lessons: Cold channels: Product Hunt, Reddit, Hacker News, vertical communities
Content SEO: ten comparison posts that capture long-tail intent
Conversion: pricing page A/B tests and cancellation save flows
Free-to-paid: the four moments that trigger upgrades

modules.title: Module 7 · Operations and compliance
modules.summary: You are live only when you can keep charging.
lessons: Refunds, chargebacks and risk handling
GDPR / CCPA: the minimum viable implementation
Revenue bookkeeping and tax basics
When to incorporate abroad — and when not to

faq.q: Can I use Stripe without an overseas company?
faq.a: Stripe requires a legal entity in a supported country. The course compares an HK/SG/US entity with Stripe against merchant-of-record options like Paddle and Lemon Squeezy, including compliance burden and stage fit.
Basic React and TypeScript. The starter repo gives you a working app; you adapt business logic and wire your own product.
Timing and minimum-budget tests are covered, but the emphasis is on free and low-cost channels because indie cash flow is fragile.

faq.q: Is it useful if I already have a product?
faq.a: Yes. Module 4 (payments) and 5 (launch) stand alone; if you have traffic but no conversion, module 6 is the one to watch.
Stripe API, auth and hosting changes are synced into courseware and the template repo; buyers get updates free.
